question: Does a vendor statement match the published MLCommons results?
row: each report lists sessions started but never sealed.
stated: a report lists every session started and not sealed
delivered: 2 of 2 scenarios refused to start B while A was open (control_abandon_A, delete_A_folder). 3 of 3 ended with "1 started, 1 sealed, 0 never sealed" with A absent (clean_A, delete_session_ledger, delete_signer_key_and_ledger)
note: compared: five local-mode scenarios: an abandoned session A, then a second session B sealed and verified. kveritas clean is documented to erase a session so that no later report lists it. Deleting the local session file or the signer key does the same. The report prints "New signer: no earlier history, other attempts cannot be ruled out" in those cases, as it does for any first report. The sibling list for a hosted seal was not tested.

delivered: 5 of 5 edits read TAMPERED: a metric value 0.8301 -> 0.9301. The invocation count 3 -> 1 (hides the failed attempt). A kept run exit code 0 -> 7. The visible page text 0.8301 -> 0.9301. The self-reported signer history, started 1 -> 9

question: Does a vendor statement match the published MLCommons results?
row: every run is recorded, failed ones too, so an attempt shows.
stated: a failed attempt shows in the report
delivered: The failed run printed "It is not kept in the report, but the server still counts it in the run history." The verify output lists Runs: 2 and no line for the failed attempt. The visible pages name no failed attempt. The embedded record holds 2 runs and an invocation count of 3
note: compared: a local-mode session with two kept runs and one failed run, sealed and verified offline. Verify prints a total of invocations only when a hosted seal supplies one (cmd/kveritas/main.go line 2305). The hosted service was not used for this row, so the sentence is not tested in the mode it describes. In local mode the failed run does not show.

delivered: A script that prints one line recorded peak GPU memory of about 12,400 MB and 100% GPU use. The source reads the system-wide ioreg counters "In use system memory" and "Device Utilization %" (internal/hardware/vendors.go lines 158 to 176)
note: compared: peak GPU memory recorded for a run that prints one line. Source read for how the counter is sampled on macOS.
